# Loop: one durable loop at a time (lock, state, heartbeat)
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #64, sha256:cbb1f0089d6b0db2378faba4f04a552f6f5942c26bcf0c834ba24c4d1f45b67d). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Done 2026-10-26 (mob-defaults 5a68227: OS-held lock, atomic state, heartbeat, resume once; suite 145 OK; the smoke run was not part of this card's Done-when and found two smoke-tool defects, see seeds)
- **Type:** tooling (thin slice; the code lives in mob-defaults; authored by the driver rotation and reviewed by a non-author under D15, with the smoke run)
- **Milestone:** process: the loop runner (retro seed P1: no turn ends with nothing running)
- **Source:** Product direction, 2026-10-26: the work should run as a loop. The continuous loop must live in the tooling, not in the facilitator's chat turns; three idle gaps today all came from the loop depending on a chat turn (retro seed P1). Team design: Decider D23 (Codex Yes, Grok Yes, Copilot Support-it with changes; agy no response).
- **Depends on:** 076 (the picker reads the GitHub board; D25)
- **Story:** As Steve, I want one durable loop to refuse duplicate starts and resume its recorded phase after interruption, so that I can trust the mob keeps working without needing a chat nudge.
- **One observable behaviour:** Starting a second loop is refused, and an interrupted loop resumes its recorded phase exactly once.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given the loop tests with the fake CLIs and a fixture board, When the behaviour above is exercised, Then a second `loop.py` exits 2 without writing anything while the OS file lock is held; the lock dies with the process, and a stale PID file is never cleared by killing anything
  2. Given the loop tests with the fake CLIs and a fixture board, When the behaviour above is exercised, Then `.mob/loop/state.json` (phase, card id, run id, attempt, last exit) is replaced atomically and written before each attempt starts; a crash mid-phase resumes that phase once
  3. Given the loop tests with the fake CLIs and a fixture board, When the behaviour above is exercised, Then `.mob/loop/heartbeat.json` (pid, phase, timestamp) is refreshed on a timer while a child runs
